title: dashboard-annotation-cookbook-for-oncall-debugging
content:
Purpose:
A compact, operator-focused cookbook for adding lightweight, structured annotations to observability dashboards so oncall and SREs can rapidly triage inference issues. This doc is intentionally prescriptive: small schema, UX knobs, sampling guidance, and rollout checklist.

Context and problem statement:
- We often rely on freeform notes in dashboards which are inconsistent and hard to query.
- During token-surge or fallback flows, engineers add ad-hoc markers that don't capture the minimal metadata needed for downstream RCA.
- Goal: make annotations cheap, consistent, and queryable while controlling trace/DB costs.

Annotation schema (minimal):
- type: [event | note | alert] (string)
- time_utc: ISO timestamp (string)
- actor: short id (oncall name or automation)
- severity: [info | warn | critical] (string)
- ticket: short id (e.g. JIRA-1234) or blank
- anchors: comma-separated tags for trace linking (e.g. span_id=abc123,session=sk42)
- model: model-name@version (string)
- kv_warmth: cold|warming|warm (string)
- quick_text: 1-2 sentence bullet for humans

UX patterns and dashboard controls:
- Compact timeline strip: show annotations as colored ticks along the top of heatmaps. Hover reveals quick_text + actor + ticket.
- Filter by severity and model: default hides info-level notes to reduce noise for paging.
- Searchable tags: anchors must conform to span labeling so clicking an anchor opens trace view pre-filtered.
- Persisted permalink: every annotation has a small permalink used in Slack and tickets.

Automated vs manual insertion:
- Manual: button in dashboard to create an annotation (keyboard shortcut). Prefill actor and time. Use type presets.
- Automated: alerting rules write annotations when probing thresholds are tripped (attach incident id). Include link to synthetic probe run id.

Sampling and retention guidance (cost-aware):
- Store full annotation metadata for 30 days (hot) then index-only for 90 days (cold).
- For high-frequency annotations (automated heartbeat events), sample 1% to long-term store and keep aggregated counts in metrics.
- When tracer sampling budget hits upper bound, prioritize traces attached to severity:critical annotations, then to severity:warn with high kv_warmth change.

Oncall recipe (quick steps):
1) Add annotation immediately when noticing user-impacting slowdown. Type=alert, severity=critical, include ticket.
2) Pin 1 example trace anchor in the note (span_id or session_id).
3) If suspected model variant issue, set model field and capture prompt sample id (anonymize before storing).
4) If KV cache suspected, set kv_warmth and record heatmap link.
5) Link annotation to escalation ticket and paste permalink into ticket comments.

Rollout checklist (instrumentation owners):
- [ ] Implement annotation API endpoint (schema above) and permissioning for write-only from alerts and dashboards.
- [ ] Add a small UI affordance on our microdash skin: keyboard shortcut, one-click annotate.
- [ ] Trace hook: map anchors to trace query params and ensure UI opens trace with correct sampling policy.
- [ ] Default retention policy and archive workflow implemented in telemetry tiering.
- [ ] Add test harness that simulates 10k annotations/day and validates sampling/aggregation.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide on exact anchor key naming convention (span_id vs trace_id vs session_id). Proposal: use span_id for single-span anchors, session_id for multi-call journeys.
- Anonymization policy for prompt snippets: minimal redaction rules needed. Work with security/compliance.
- Cost cap thresholds — coordinate with finance to pin retention costs per tenant.

Notes to implementers (short tips):
- Keep the annotation payload small; avoid freeform blobs.
- Use normalized enums to enable efficient index filters.
- Prefer adding links to off-platform artifacts (ticket, slack thread) instead of embedding long content.

Examples (short):
- Manual critical: {type:alert, time_utc:2025-03-01T14:12:03Z, actor:ava, severity:critical, ticket:JIRA-OPS-942, anchors:span_id=ok7f9, model:guanaco-7B@v2, kv_warmth:cold, quick_text:"large latency spike after deploy, many 504s"}
- Automated info: {type:event, time_utc:2025-03-01T14:00:00Z, actor:synthetic-probe, severity:info, ticket:, anchors:probe=kanary-3, model:opt-3b@q4, kv_warmth:warm, quick_text:"routine probe: p99 within SLO"}

If you take this forward, next immediate step: small prototype toolbar for the investigation microdash that lets me add an annotation and copies the permalink to clipboard. Ping Ravi and Lena for UX + trace-API mapping.

End.
